note: The Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia (established 1080 by Armenian refugees fleeing Seljuk conquest of Armenia proper) maintained complex relations with Byzantium, oscillating between cooperation (the Armenians provided crucial infantry for crusading armies) and conflict (Byzantine emperors periodically attempted to reassert suzerainty over Cilicia). The Armenian-Byzantine relationship was complicated by theological differences (Armenian Apostolic vs. Greek Orthodox Christianity). Armenian Cilicia aligned with the Crusader states and with the Mongol Ilkhanate against the Mamluks, ultimately being abandoned by both and destroyed by the Mamluks (1375).

_quarry.structural_significance: Armenian Cilicia serves as a crucial bridge between the Crusader states and Anatolia; Armenian support for the Crusades (providing local knowledge, logistical support, troops) is an underappreciated factor in crusading military capacity; the kingdom's destruction by the Mamluks ends the last surviving Armenian state until the 20th century
